issues.description: Fields numberOfInscribedStudents and numberOfGuestStudents have conflicting types across artifacts. In the problem statement UML (problem_statement.md lines 65-66) both fields are declared as type double, while the reference implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java lines 6-10) declares them as int. The UML in the problem statement also shows getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int (problem_statement.md line 70), which implies integer arithmetic. This mismatch (double vs int) is likely to confuse students about which type to implement and may lead to compilation or test-signature mismatches if they follow the UML instead of the example solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the types consistent between the problem statement UML and the code. Preferred fix: update the UML in problem_statement.md to declare numberOfInscribedStudents and numberOfGuestStudents as int (to match the reference solution and the getTotalNumberOfStudents() return type). Alternatively, if fractional students are intended, change the solution and UML method signatures to use double consistently (including getTotalNumberOfStudents() returning double) and update example code and text accordingly.
